# dtgsna

> Estimates reciprocal condition numbers for eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a generalized Schur form.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dtgsna from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dtgsna';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dtgsna(
    order,
    job, howmny,
    SELECT, strideSELECT,
    N,
    A, LDA,
    B, LDB,
    VL, LDVL,
    VR, LDVR,
    s, strideS,
    DIF, strideDIF,
    mm,
    M,
    WORK,
    IWORK
) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `job` | `"eigenvalues" \| "eigenvectors" \| "both"` | Specifies the operation type<br>One of `'both'`, `'eigenvalues'`, `'eigenvectors'`. |
| `howmny` | `"all" \| "selected"` | Specifies the operation type<br>One of `'all'`, `'selected'`. |
| `SELECT` | `Uint8Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Input array |
| ↳ `strideSELECT` | `integer` | Stride length for `SELECT` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `B` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `B`<br>Requires `LDB ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `VL` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × mm</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDVL` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `VL`<br>Rejects `(job === 'eigenvalues' \|\| job === 'both') && ldvl < N` |
| `VR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × mm</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDVR` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `VR`<br>Rejects `(job === 'eigenvalues' \|\| job === 'both') && ldvr < N` |
| `s` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length mm</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideS` | `integer` | Stride length for `s` |
| `DIF` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length mm</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideDIF` | `integer` | Stride length for `DIF` |
| `mm` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of elements in the arrays S and DIF. |
| `M` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Number of rows |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ LWMIN</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| `IWORK` | `Int32Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ N + 6</sub> | **out** · Output array |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `job`: Specifies whether condition numbers are required for eigenvalues (S) or eigenvectors (`DIF`):

  -   `= 'E'`: for eigenvalues only (S);
  -   `= 'V'`: for eigenvectors only (`DIF`);
  -   `= 'B'`: for both eigenvalues and eigenvectors (S and `DIF`).
- `howmny`:

  -   `= 'A'`: compute condition numbers for all eigenpairs;
  -   `= 'S'`: compute condition numbers for selected eigenpairs specified by the array `SELECT`.
- `SELECT`: If `HOWMNY = 'S'`, `SELECT` specifies the eigenpairs for which condition numbers are required. To select condition numbers for the eigenpair corresponding to a real eigenvalue w(j), `SELECT(j)` must be set to .TRUE.. To select condition numbers corresponding to a complex conjugate pair of eigenvalues w(j) and w(j+1), either `SELECT(j)` or `SELECT(j+1)` or both, must be set to .TRUE.. If `HOWMNY = 'A'`, `SELECT` is not referenced.
- `N`: The order of the square matrix pair (A, B). $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: The upper quasi-triangular matrix A in the pair (A,B).
- `B`: The upper triangular matrix B in the pair (A,B).
- `VL`: If `JOB = 'E'` or 'B', `VL` must contain left eigenvectors of (A, B), corresponding to the eigenpairs specified by `HOWMNY` and `SELECT`. The eigenvectors must be stored in consecutive columns of `VL`, as returned by DTGEVC. If `JOB = 'V'`, `VL` is not referenced.
- `VR`: If `JOB = 'E'` or 'B', `VR` must contain right eigenvectors of (A, B), corresponding to the eigenpairs specified by `HOWMNY` and `SELECT`. The eigenvectors must be stored in consecutive columns ov `VR`, as returned by DTGEVC. If `JOB = 'V'`, `VR` is not referenced.
- `s`: If `JOB = 'E'` or 'B', the reciprocal condition numbers of the selected eigenvalues, stored in consecutive elements of the array. For a complex conjugate pair of eigenvalues two consecutive elements of S are set to the same value. Thus `S(j)`, `DIF(j)`, and the j-th columns of `VL` and `VR` all correspond to the same eigenpair (but not in general the j-th eigenpair, unless all eigenpairs are selected). If `JOB = 'V'`, S is not referenced.
- `DIF`: If `JOB = 'V'` or 'B', the estimated reciprocal condition numbers of the selected eigenvectors, stored in consecutive elements of the array. For a complex eigenvector two consecutive elements of `DIF` are set to the same value. If the eigenvalues cannot be reordered to compute `DIF(j)`, `DIF(j)` is set to 0; this can only occur when the true value would be very small anyway. If `JOB = 'E'`, `DIF` is not referenced.
- `mm`: The number of elements in the arrays S and `DIF`. $\mathrm{MM} \ge M$.
- `M`: The number of elements of the arrays S and `DIF` used to store the specified condition numbers; for each selected real eigenvalue one element is used, and for each selected complex conjugate pair of eigenvalues, two elements are used. If `HOWMNY = 'A'`, M is set to N.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.
- `IWORK`: If `JOB = 'E'`, `IWORK` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "both", "eigenvalues", "eigenvectors"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "all", "selected"
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` tenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` twelfth argument is invalid (column-major: rejected when `( job === "eigenvalues" \|\| job === "both" ) && LDVL < N`)
- `RangeError` twelfth argument is invalid (row-major: rejected when `( job === "eigenvalues" \|\| job === "both" ) && LDVL < max( 1, mm )`)
- `RangeError` fourteenth argument is invalid (column-major: rejected when `( job === "eigenvalues" \|\| job === "both" ) && LDVR < N`)
- `RangeError` fourteenth argument is invalid (row-major: rejected when `( job === "eigenvalues" \|\| job === "both" ) && LDVR < max( 1, mm )`)
- `RangeError` leading dimensions must satisfy LDA, LDB, LDVL, LDVR >= max(1, N)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dtgsna.ndarray(
    job, howmny,
    SELECT, strideSELECT, offsetSELECT,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    VL, strideVL1, strideVL2, offsetVL,
    VR, strideVR1, strideVR2, offsetVR,
    s, strideS, offsetS,
    DIF, strideDIF, offsetDIF,
    mm,
    M,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    IWORK, strideIWork, offsetIWork
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `job` | `"eigenvalues" \| "eigenvectors" \| "both"` | Specifies the operation type<br>One of `'both'`, `'eigenvalues'`, `'eigenvectors'`. |
| `howmny` | `"all" \| "selected"` | Specifies the operation type<br>One of `'all'`, `'selected'`. |
| `SELECT` | `Uint8Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Input array |
| ↳ `strideSELECT` | `integer` | Stride length for `SELECT` |
| ↳ `offsetSELECT` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `SELECT` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of columns<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `A` |
| `B` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `B` |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `B` |
| `VL` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × mm</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideVL1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `VL` |
| ↳ `strideVL2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `VL` |
| ↳ `offsetVL` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `VL` |
| `VR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × mm</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideVR1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `VR` |
| ↳ `strideVR2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `VR` |
| ↳ `offsetVR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `VR` |
| `s` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length mm</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideS` | `integer` | Stride length for `s` |
| ↳ `offsetS` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `s` |
| `DIF` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length mm</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideDIF` | `integer` | Stride length for `DIF` |
| ↳ `offsetDIF` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `DIF` |
| `mm` | `NonNegativeInteger` | The number of elements in the arrays S and DIF. |
| `M` | `Int32Array` | **out** · Number of rows |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ LWMIN</sub> | **out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `WORK` |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `WORK` |
| `IWORK` | `Int32Array`<br><sub>length ≥ N + 6</sub> | **out** · Output array |
| ↳ `strideIWork` | `integer` | Stride length for `IWORK` |
| ↳ `offsetIWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `IWORK` |

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "both", "eigenvalues", "eigenvectors"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "all", "selected"

- `RangeError` `N` must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` `IWORK` must have at least `N + 6` elements from `offsetIWork`

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `=0`: Successful exit
-   `<0`: If `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dtgsna()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DTGSNA`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dtgsna.f).
-   The routine assumes the matrix pair `(A,B)` is already in generalized real Schur canonical form (upper quasi-triangular `A`, upper triangular `B`).
-   For `job='eigenvalues'` or `'both'`, the left and right eigenvectors `VL` and `VR` must be provided (e.g. from `dtgevc`).
-   The workspace must satisfy `lwork >= 2*N*(N+2)+16` when `job='eigenvectors'` or `'both'`; otherwise `lwork >= N` suffices.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import Uint8Array from '@stdlib/array/uint8/lib/index.js';
import dtgsna from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dtgsna';

const N = 3;
const A = new Float64Array( N * N );
const B = new Float64Array( N * N );
const VL = new Float64Array( N * N );
const VR = new Float64Array( N * N );
const s = new Float64Array( N );
const DIF = new Float64Array( N );
const WORK = new Float64Array( ( 2 * N * ( N + 2 ) ) + 16 );
const IWORK = new Int32Array( N + 6 );
const SELECT = new Uint8Array( N );
const M = new Int32Array( 1 );

A[ 0 ] = 1.0;
A[ 3 ] = 0.5;
A[ 4 ] = 2.0;
A[ 6 ] = 0.3;
A[ 7 ] = 0.4;
A[ 8 ] = 3.0;

B[ 0 ] = 1.0;
B[ 3 ] = 0.2;
B[ 4 ] = 1.5;
B[ 6 ] = 0.1;
B[ 7 ] = 0.3;
B[ 8 ] = 2.0;

VL[ 0 ] = 1.0;
VL[ 4 ] = 1.0;
VL[ 8 ] = 1.0;
VR[ 0 ] = 1.0;
VR[ 4 ] = 1.0;
VR[ 8 ] = 1.0;

dtgsna.ndarray( 'both', 'all', SELECT, 1, 0, N, A, 1, N, 0, B, 1, N, 0, VL, 1, N, 0, VR, 1, N, 0, s, 1, 0, DIF, 1, 0, N, M, WORK, 1, 0, IWORK, 1, 0 );

console.log( 's =', s ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'DIF =', DIF ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'M =', M[ 0 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DTGSNA`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DTGSNA estimates reciprocal condition numbers for specified eigenvalues and/or eigenvectors of a matrix pair (A, B) in generalized real Schur canonical form (or of any matrix pair $(Q \, A \, Z^T, Q \, B \, Z^T)$ with orthogonal matrices Q and Z, where $Z^T$ denotes the transpose of Z.

(A, B) must be in generalized real Schur form (as returned by DGGES), i.e. A is block upper triangular with 1-by-1 and 2-by-2 diagonal blocks. B is upper triangular.

### Further Details

The reciprocal of the condition number of a generalized eigenvalue $w = (a, b)$ is defined as

`S(w)` = (\|$u^{\mathrm{TAv}}$\|\*\*2 + \|$u^{\mathrm{TBv}}$\|\*\*2)\*\*(1/2) / (norm(u)\*norm(v))

where u and v are the left and right eigenvectors of (A, B) corresponding to w; \|z\| denotes the absolute value of the complex number, and norm(u) denotes the 2-norm of the vector u. The pair (a, b) corresponds to an eigenvalue $w = a/b$ (= $u^{\mathrm{TAv}}/u^{\mathrm{TBv}}$) of the matrix pair (A, B). If both a and b equal zero, then (A B) is singular and $S(I) = -1$ is returned.

An approximate error bound on the chordal distance between the i-th computed generalized eigenvalue w and the corresponding exact eigenvalue $\lambda$ is

chord(w, $\lambda$) \<= $\mathrm{EPS} \, \operatorname{norm}(A, B) / S(I)$

where EPS is the machine precision.

The reciprocal of the condition number `DIF(i)` of right eigenvector u and left eigenvector v corresponding to the generalized eigenvalue w is defined as follows:

a) If the i-th eigenvalue $w = (a,b)$ is real

Suppose U and V are orthogonal transformations such that

```text
U**T*(A, B)*V  = (S, T) = ( a   *  ) ( b  *  )  1
                          ( 0  S22 ),( 0 T22 )  n-1
                            1  n-1     1 n-1
```

Then the reciprocal condition number `DIF(i)` is

Difl((a, b), (S22, T22)) = $\sigma$-min( Zl ),

where $\sigma$-min(Zl) denotes the smallest singular value of the 2(n-1)-by-2(n-1) matrix

Zl = \[ kron(a, In-1) -kron(1, S22) \]

\[ kron(b, In-1) -kron(1, T22) \] .

Here In-1 is the identity matrix of size n-1. kron(X, Y) is the Kronecker product between the matrices X and Y.

Note that if the default method for computing `DIF(i)` is wanted (see DLATDF), then the parameter DIFDRI (see below) should be changed from 3 to 4 (routine DLATDF($\mathrm{IJOB} = 2$ will be used)). See DTGSYL for more details.

b) If the i-th and (i+1)-th eigenvalues are complex conjugate pair,

Suppose U and V are orthogonal transformations such that

$U^T \, (A, B) \, V = (S, T) = ( S_{11} \, )$ ( T11 \* ) 2

```text
( 0    S22 ),( 0    T22) n-2
  2    n-2     2    n-2
```

and (S11, T11) corresponds to the complex conjugate eigenvalue pair (w, conjg(w)). There exist unitary matrices U1 and V1 such that

$$
U_{1}^T \, S_{11} \, V_{1} = \begin{pmatrix} s_{11} & s_{12} \\ 0 & s_{22} \end{pmatrix} \quad\text{and}\quad U_{1}^T \, T_{11} \, V_{1} = \begin{pmatrix} t_{11} & t_{12} \\ 0 & t_{22} \end{pmatrix}
$$

```text
where the generalized eigenvalues w = s11/t11 and
conjg(w) = s22/t22.
```

Then the reciprocal condition number `DIF(i)` is bounded by

$$
\min ( d_{1}, \max ( 1, |\operatorname{real}(s_{11})/\operatorname{real}(s_{22})| ) \, d_{2} )
$$

where, d1 = Difl((s11, t11), (s22, t22)) = $\sigma$-min(Z1), where Z1 is the complex 2-by-2 matrix

$$
Z_{1} = \begin{bmatrix} s_{11} & -s_{22} \\ t_{11} & -t_{22} \end{bmatrix}
$$

This is done by computing (using real arithmetic) the roots of the characteristical polynomial $\det (Z_{1}^T \, Z_{1} - \lambda I)$, where $Z_{1}^T$ denotes the transpose of Z1 and det(X) denotes the determinant of X.

and d2 is an upper bound on Difl((S11, T11), (S22, T22)), i.e. an upper bound on $\sigma$-min(Z2), where Z2 is (2n-2)-by-(2n-2)

Z2 = \[ kron($S_{11}^T$, In-2) -kron(I2, S22) \]

\[ kron($T_{11}^T$, In-2) -kron(I2, T22) \]

Note that if the default method for computing `DIF` is wanted (see DLATDF), then the parameter DIFDRI (see below) should be changed from 3 to 4 (routine DLATDF($\mathrm{IJOB} = 2$ will be used)). See DTGSYL for more details.

For each eigenvalue/vector specified by `SELECT`, `DIF` stores a Frobenius norm-based estimate of Difl.

An approximate error bound for the i-th computed eigenvector `VL(i)` or `VR(i)` is given by

$$
\mathrm{EPS} \, \operatorname{norm}(A, B) / \mathrm{DIF}(i)
$$

See ref. \[2-3\] for more details and further references.

### References

\[2\] B. Kagstrom and P. Poromaa; Computing Eigenspaces with Specified

-   Eigenvalues of a Regular Matrix Pair (A, B) and Condition
-   Estimation: Theory, Algorithms and Software,
-   Report UMINF - 94.04, Department of Computing Science, Umea
-   University, S-901 87 Umea, Sweden, 1994. Also as LAPACK Working
-   Note 87. To appear in Numerical Algorithms, 1996.

\[3\] B. Kagstrom and P. Poromaa, LAPACK-Style Algorithms and Software

-   for Solving the Generalized Sylvester Equation and Estimating the
-   Separation between Regular Matrix Pairs, Report UMINF - 93.23,
-   Department of Computing Science, Umea University, S-901 87 Umea,
